rows.title: BEST OF 2024: CT state agencies ordered to tally unspent ARPA funds
rows.standfirst: The directive from Gov. Lamont’s budget director was issued hours after The Connecticut Mirror published a story about legislators’ concerns.

rows.title: Critics, backers of CT’s budget ‘guardrails’ want transparent debate
rows.standfirst: Both supporters of CT’s ‘fiscal guardrails’ and reform advocates agree on one thing: They want the debate to play out in the light of day.

rows.title: Treasurer: CT saves big by not stashing transportation funds
rows.standfirst: CT Treasurer Erick Russell said he will ask legislators to cap the Special Transportation Fund’s emergency reserve at 18% of the STF.

rows.title: CT Gov. Lamont’s ‘north stars’ in 2025: opportunity and affordability
rows.standfirst: Gov. Ned Lamont will offer suggestions to open discussion, but he won’t likely address pressure to revise the state’s fiscal guardrails.

rows.title: Lamont assures CBIA that CT’s spending cap is ‘sacrosanct’
rows.standfirst: Gov. Ned Lamont told business leaders he won’t touch the spending cap, but left room for debate on other fiscal guardrails.

rows.title: Big interest earnings from COVID grants were kept out of CT budget since 2021
rows.standfirst: The Treasurer’s Office did not properly move the interest earnings to CT’s General Fund until a few weeks ago, Lamont’s budget director said.

rows.title: What will Trump mean for CT’s fiscal future? Lawmakers are wary
rows.standfirst: Washington gives CT billions of dollars annually, and lawmakers are watching how Trump could affect Medicaid, transit projects and education.

rows.title: Poll: Voters say CT must spend more on K-12 education
rows.standfirst: CT voters are satisfied with the quality of public schools but most believe the state should cover more of the cost, according to a new poll.

rows.title: Is Lamont the key to reforming CT’s ‘fiscal guardrails’?
rows.standfirst: Reformers hope to mimic legal maneuvers that Gov. Ned Lamont employed five years ago to free up money for social services and other programs.

rows.title: CT’s free-spending past leaves some wary of easing budget caps
rows.standfirst: The last time Connecticut’s revenues boomed, the state spent far more than it saved. Some conservatives fear Democrats will repeat the past.

rows.title: With federal funding in limbo, CT Dems propose Medicaid expansion
rows.standfirst: CT Dems unveiled a $250M plan to raise Medicaid reimbursement rates, saying ‘we can’t stop doing our jobs’ amid federal funding uncertainty.
